stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and describes a complex multi-platform CMS live preview feature (GO, UP, MX). openspec must run first to elaborate requirements and draft meaningful ACs; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage. Both agents assigned due to complexity and criticality.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story: Live Preview capability does not exist in the codebase. The primary attachment point is useContent (236 callers), which is the single gateway for content fetching. All Contentstack components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) consume content through this hook and would inherit preview behavior once it's supported. Acceptance criteria were empty; VCs derived from the description alone.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all ACs are derived from the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' and the technical file paths. The paths (useContent.ts with 236 callers, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink) informed the architectural inference that preview flows through the existing content hook and service layer. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I do not have the file contents — my ACs are based on architectural inference from paths and the Contentstack Live Preview paradigm alone. If useContent.ts or contentstack.ts have existing patterns (e.g., caching, retry logic, locale handling) that conflict with these ACs, they may need adjustment. AC-3 and AC-8 ensure zero regression in non-preview mode. AC-9 and AC-15 address security (expired tokens, cross-tab leakage). AC-4, AC-5, AC-6, AC-16 cover error and edge cases. AC-18 covers accessibility. AC-13 and AC-14 provide a user-facing preview indicator with exit capability. AC-12 covers localization. AC-17 covers referenced content resolution.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents ran but neither persisted acceptance criteria (acceptanceChanged: false for both, splitCount: 0). Openspec correctly identified the novel nature of the story and the primary attachment point (useContent with 236 callers), providing useful architectural grounding. Speckit outlined a comprehensive AC framework in its notes (security, edge cases, accessibility, localization, regression safety) — but explicitly caveated that it never read the actual file contents and based all ACs on 'architectural inference from paths' alone. For a complex multi-platform CMS live preview feature touching 236 callers of the central content hook, inference-only spec work is insufficient. The described ACs (AC-3 through AC-18) appear thoughtful but were not written back to the story. Human review is needed to verify that the inferred ACs align with existing patterns in useContent.ts and contentstack.ts, and to ensure the ACs are actually persisted.
